title: Precision intake telemetry bridge and pin safeguards for low-precision model variants
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a robust telemetry bridge and pin-safeguard workflow to onboard INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ variants with deterministic performance fingerprints and automated regression detection. The goal is to make variant intake safe for runtime rollouts: produce signed performance artifacts, canonicalize telemetry events for perf/latency/cost/quality, wire a lightweight canary detector that compares live fingerprint against baseline, and ensure model-version pins propagate atomically across control-plane and serving runtime. This ticket covers the ingestion side (artifact signing + metadata), runtime hooks for fingerprint collection (latency histograms, token-per-cost, kv-cache hit rates, micro-batching shape), and the observability contract and alerting rules needed for automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Signed performance artifact (manifest.json + signature) emitted for each variant build and stored in model-artifact-bucket
Telemetry schema v2 implemented and agreed by infra/observability teams; example events produced by staging canary
Canary detector runs as a scheduled job and flags deviations beyond configured thresholds (latency P95, generation quality metrics, cost-per-token)
Model pin propagation end-to-end: pin published in control-plane -> pinned hash used by dedicated and private runtimes within 5 minutes
Automated rollback hook exercised in staging against a simulated regression and documented in runbook

notes: Decision: use dual-signature model for artifact manifests (build-signer + control-plane-signer) to prevent accidental rollout of unsigned variants.
Tradeoff: collecting detailed per-token traces increases telemetry cost; initial rollout will sample 1% of requests and aggregate histograms to reduce overhead.
Next: unblock ENG-40227 (KMS binding) to complete e2e artifact signing. Scheduled pairing with Security on 2026-03-12.
